clue.text: Compassionate chap, in tone

indicators.note: the chap is placed inside the word for tone, as the clue's 'in' directs

parts.note: a hue is a shade or tone of colour
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A kindly fellow who speaks in a gentle tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humane shows kindness and mercy, which is what being compassionate means; a direct synonym.

clue.text: This garment's been ruined by acid, gran!

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are knocked out of order and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Granny's knitwear has been spoilt by a spill of acid.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jacket that buttons down the front, an example of a garment.

clue.text: Accepting the directors' recommendations and getting ignored

definitions.meaning: read literally, going along with what the board of directors proposes
the idiom means being neglected or abandoned, like something fallen overboard

explanation.surface: A shareholder who simply nods through whatever the board wants, and is then overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being dropped or disregarded; the first definition plays on a company board's directors.

clue.text: Reprimand after short time gets one weeping

indicators.note: the reprimand comes after the short time, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
an earful is a scolding or telling-off

explanation.surface: After a quick dressing-down, somebody bursts into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearful describes someone crying or close to it, a straightforward synonym of weeping.

clue.text: A noted graduate?

parts.note: noted seems to mean famous, but here it means dealing in musical notes: a graduate with a degree in that subject

explanation.definitionFit: This is the degree title of someone who has graduated in music, the subject of notes and scores.

clue.text: Knight's advantage having collected a wife

indicators.note: the advantage gathers up the other letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a gain is a benefit or advantage
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A knight wins an edge in life by marrying.
explanation.walkthrough: Gawain is one of King Arthur's Knights of the Round Table, famous from the poem Sir Gawain and the Green Knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain is a knight of Arthurian legend, so the definition gives an example category for him.

clue.text: One usually has ten big books, not a thousand!

indicators.note: the thousand is not wanted, so it is removed from the books

parts.note: tomes are large heavy books
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A remark that big volumes usually come in sets of ten, but not a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a person usually has ten toes, though the surface has us counting books.
explanation.definitionFit: A person normally has ten of these digits on their feet, a playful descriptive definition.

clue.text: Young animal, a form of insect

parts.note: a pup is a young dog, seal or similar animal

explanation.surface: A young creature that is also an insect at one stage of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa is the inactive stage of an insect between larva and adult, a form it takes.

clue.text: Something to be deciphered, not the first poem

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a code is something one must decipher

explanation.surface: A poem presented as a puzzle that needs cracking.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, usually addressing a subject; a direct example of a poem.

clue.text: A tortuous route cut short on river

indicators.note: the word for the route loses its last letter

parts.note: a maze is a winding, confusing path

explanation.surface: A winding journey abandoned partway along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is the great river of South America, an example of a river.

clue.text: Anger shown by chaps blocking a theologian

indicators.note: the chaps surround the other letters, closing them in as a block would

parts.note: men are chaps
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Fury when a group of men stand in a theologian's way.
explanation.definitionFit: To madden someone is to enrage or infuriate them, a direct verb synonym of anger.

clue.text: Practise with special vehicle about to start

indicators.note: the word for about is placed at the beginning

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a hearse is the special vehicle that carries a coffin

explanation.surface: Getting in some practice with an unusual vehicle that is about to set off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to go through something for practice before performing it, a synonym of practise.

clue.text: Insensible, rough — otherwise showing a helpful disposition!

indicators.note: the letters are arranged otherwise, in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone numb and rough, or else kind and helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neighbourly means friendly and helpful to those nearby, so the abstract noun is a helpful disposition.

clue.text: Mentioned one being put out and far from happy

indicators.note: the one is ejected from the word for mentioned

parts.note: said means mentioned
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone said to have been ejected and now unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sad is the opposite of being happy, so far from happy is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Powerful type with a good name, friend to have around

indicators.note: the friend goes around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: An influential figure of good reputation whose pal stays close.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a wealthy and influential businessperson, someone powerful.

clue.text: Wood — find some hyenas here

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: An invitation to spot hyenas in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a tree whose timber is used for tool handles, so it names a kind of wood.

clue.text: Team getting silver about to be embraced by woman at match

indicators.note: the silver goes inside the woman, held as in an embrace

parts.note: a bride is the woman at a match, in the sense of a marriage

indicators.note: about means the word for silver is turned round

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A team winning silver, with a woman at the game hugging a teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport, but here it is a marriage. 'about' turns AG into GA.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is an organised group, as in a fire brigade, so it can mean a team.

clue.text: Good, like certain yarns, keeping one engaged

parts.note: a ripping yarn is an exciting story, a dated British phrase

explanation.surface: Good stories of a certain kind hold the attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gripping holds the attention firmly, keeping one absorbed or engaged.

clue.text: Like certain cross people living on a Mediterranean island

definitions.meaning: a ... cross is the eight-pointed cross of the Knights Hospitaller

definitions.text: people living on a Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: Grumpy islanders in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the eight-pointed cross and the natives of the island of Malta.

clue.text: Eager Cardiff has excited diplomat

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic Welsh capital has an agitated envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargé d'affaires is a diplomat who stands in for an ambassador or heads a minor mission.

clue.text: Despicable type submerging animal under river

indicators.note: in this down clue the animal goes below the river

parts.note: an otter is a water-loving animal

explanation.surface: A nasty person drowning a creature beneath a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is a dated British term for a contemptible, unpleasant person.

clue.text: Old lover, one shown the way and deported

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
I is the Roman numeral for one
led means guided or shown the way

explanation.surface: A former partner, escorted out and thrown out of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exiled is to be banished from one's country, close in meaning to deported.

clue.text: Insect gets to scamper around little old vegetable

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: the word for scamper wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: to trot is to run at a brisk pace
O is a little, abbreviated, form of old

explanation.surface: A bug runs rapidly round a small, old vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetroot is a dark red root vegetable, so the definition names its category.

clue.text: On the radio employ sheep

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to use is to employ

explanation.surface: A broadcast announcement about hiring sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewes are female sheep, so the plural noun matches the definition.

clue.text: Like voluntary work with international organisation, quiet help

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
p is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet
aid is help

explanation.surface: Volunteering with a global body, giving help quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Voluntary work is done without wages, so it is by nature not paid.

clue.text: Superficial quality of archdeacon, always poetic

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: An archdeacon who is forever writing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin outer layer, and figuratively a surface show hiding what is beneath.

clue.text: Participate in sport — almost miss out

indicators.note: almost the whole word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: to skip is to miss out or omit

explanation.surface: Joining in the sport, but very nearly not turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ski is to take part in the sport of skiing, a verb for participating in it.

clue.text: Want to be kicked, do we hear?

indicators.note: asking what we hear signals the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: kneed means struck with the knee, like being kicked

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone really wants a kicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Need and want are synonyms as nouns or verbs: to lack something one requires.
